metadata.requirement_prompt: Design an enterprise agile project management desktop dashboard for software teams with sprint kanban, pull request traceability, and velocity burndown charts

preflight.summary: Context sufficiency score: 65%. Sufficient context to proceed with autonomous synthesis.
preflight.identified_intent: Collaborative team project and task management workspace

clarification_questions.question: What specific tasks should the user be able to perform?
clarification_questions.rationale: User flows and screen inventories cannot be derived without key task verbs.
suggested_answers: Search, select, checkout, and live track
Create projects, assign tasks, track kanban status

confirmed_facts.snippet: Design an enterprise agile project management desktop dashboard for software teams with sprint kanban, pull request traceability, and velocity burndown charts

explicit_assumptions.statement: Developers prefer a dual Kanban/List toggle rather than forced board views.
explicit_assumptions.basis: Engineers scanning backlog prefer dense lists; standup reviews prefer board columns.

explicit_assumptions.statement: A collapsible contextual sidebar preserves screen real-estate on 13-inch laptop displays.
explicit_assumptions.basis: Minimizes cognitive friction when viewing wide 6-column kanban boards.

ux_architecture.product_purpose: Empower agile engineering teams to plan sprints, track pull-requests and task progress, assign work without cognitive overhead, and maintain clear velocity.

personas.name: Marcus Vance - Lead Staff Engineer
personas.primary_goal: Keep a 10-person distributed backend team unblocked and track sprint commitments without spending hours updating Jira.
core_needs: Instant visibility into pull-request status and blocked dependencies
Keyboard-first task creation and status changes
Automated sprint burndown telemetry without manual ticket grooming
pain_points: Bloated enterprise project tools requiring 15 clicks just to create a subtask
Out-of-sync task states because engineers hate updating slow tools
Fragmented context between Slack, GitHub, and task boards
personas.context_of_use: Dual 4K desktop workstation, Chrome and terminal windows open side-by-side.
personas.mental_model: Linear, GitHub Projects, or Raycast: speed, keyboard navigation, clean aesthetics.

personas.name: Elena Rostova - Full-Stack Developer
personas.primary_goal: Pick up assigned sprint tickets, understand requirements immediately, and link Git PRs with zero friction.
core_needs: Clean markdown descriptions with code snippet highlighting
Clear priority labels and acceptance criteria checklists
Fast filter to 'My Tasks' in 1 click
pain_points: Ambiguous ticket descriptions with no clear definition of done
Losing focus due to clunky UI lag during sprint planning meetings
personas.context_of_use: MacBook Pro 14-inch, IDE active, prefers Dark Mode.
personas.mental_model: Task board as an extension of the developer Git workflow.

jtbd_list.situation: When conducting Monday morning sprint planning with my team
jtbd_list.motivation: I want to quickly assign unestimated backlog items and visualize team capacity
jtbd_list.expected_outcome: So the sprint is committed in 20 minutes without lingering ambiguity
jtbd_list.success_metric: Sprint setup completed in under 15 minutes; story point allocation verified

jtbd_list.situation: When finishing a feature branch commit in my terminal
jtbd_list.motivation: I want the task status to automatically flip from 'In Progress' to 'In Review'
jtbd_list.expected_outcome: So I don't have to manually context-switch into another browser tab
jtbd_list.success_metric: Zero manual status updates required for linked PRs

primary_journey.title: Sprint Execution & Task Lifecycle

phases.friction_risk: Drowning in hundreds of stale tickets across unorganized columns
phases.mitigation_strategy: High-contrast 'Blocked Items' summary badge and instant search filter

phases.user_thought: 'Need to file an urgent bug fix for auth token expiration.'
phases.friction_risk: Lengthy modal form with 20 compulsory enterprise fields
phases.mitigation_strategy: Streamlined modal: Title, Priority, Assignee, Markdown Body; 'Cmd+Enter' to save

phases.user_thought: 'Moving this to Done now that CI checks passed.'
phases.friction_risk: Laggy drag-and-drop or lost status updates
phases.mitigation_strategy: Fluid drag feedback with optimistic UI update and keyboard shortcut 'M' to move

phases.user_thought: 'Did we hit our velocity target this fortnight?'
phases.friction_risk: Convoluted data tables with no actionable burnup trend line
phases.mitigation_strategy: Clear visual burnup chart with completed vs scope-creep delta indicators

primary_journey.entry_point: Open browser dashboard at morning standup
primary_journey.success_state: Team completes sprint on schedule with full PR traceability

key_mental_models: Keyboard mastery: Engineers expect 'Cmd+K' command palettes and hotkeys over mouse navigation.
Dense scannability: Prefer compact 32px table rows and column chips over airy consumer whitespace.

primary_risks: Changing task status interaction may disrupt established muscle-memory during standups.
Automated Git PR linking might surprise engineers if tickets update without explicit confirmation.
New analytics dashboard adds visual weight to the sidebar navigation.
progressive_disclosure_steps: Step 1: Baseline Entry - Keep standard Kanban drag-and-drop identical to existing agile boards.
Step 2: Contextual Teaser - When task is moved to 'In Review', prompt: 'Link branch feat/auth? [Link once] [Always auto-link]'.
Step 3: Advanced Controls - Velocity burndown charts live in dedicated 'Analytics' tab rather than cluttering daily board.
non_disruptive_strategy.opt_in_toggle_spec: Settings > Workflow > 'Enable automated GitHub status transitions' (Default: Opt-in with confirmation banner).
non_disruptive_strategy.contextual_onboarding_trigger: Show non-modal toast when first commit with issue key ENG-xxx is pushed: 'We detected a linked commit! Click to view status update.'.

safe_fallbacks.failure_trigger: GitHub Webhook or CI status API rate-limited
safe_fallbacks.fallback_behavior: Allow manual drag status change with an informational indicator: 'PR status check delayed'.
safe_fallbacks.user_messaging: Git sync is running slow. You can still move tasks manually.

safe_fallbacks.failure_trigger: Engineer accidentally moves card to 'Done' prematurely
safe_fallbacks.fallback_behavior: Provide instant 'Undo' floating snackbar for 8 seconds and log undo action in task history.

findings.title: Explicit verification required before high-value action
findings.problem: User might tap confirmation accidentally when moving quickly.
findings.why_it_matters: Accidental submissions cause immediate user panic, refund requests, or phantom tickets.
findings.ux_principle: Nielsen Heuristic #5: Error Prevention (Slips and Mistakes)
findings.recommendation: Use explicit swipe-to-confirm affordance or 8-second undo snackbar.

findings.title: Preserve previous search filters and recent location memory
findings.problem: Users frequently re-enter the exact same dietary filter or sprint squad view.
findings.why_it_matters: Forcing recall rather than recognition increases cognitive friction.
findings.evidence: Observed default filter reset on screen revisit.
findings.ux_principle: Nielsen Heuristic #6: Recognition Rather Than Recall
findings.recommendation: Store top 3 recent selections in local cache with 1-tap re-activation.
findings.validation_test: Track filter click frequency in product analytics.

findings.title: Real-time ETA and courier milestone synchronization
findings.problem: Static progress bars create anxiety if status doesn't refresh within 30 seconds.
findings.why_it_matters: Users wonder if the system stalled or network disconnected.
findings.ux_principle: Nielsen Heuristic #1: Visibility of System Status
findings.recommendation: Include subtle pulsing live indicator and 'Updated 5s ago' timestamp.
findings.validation_test: User anxiety feedback survey during active orders.

audit_report.mentor_summary: Overall UX health is strong at 88/100. Found 1 high-priority friction point around error prevention. Address the confirmation affordance to make this bulletproof for distracted users!
